Findings
[P1] Make can skip Bazel after source edits
The new archive rules depend only on .platform and _BAZEL_BASE archives. After the first build, editing a source used by the Bazel container leaves those prerequisites unchanged. Make considers the existing .gz current and skips bazel run, potentially carrying stale container contents into the final image. This affects release and debug builds. [Bazel archive rules](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/slave.mk#L1507-L1517)
The outer Make’s -B does not solve this: it is not forwarded through Docker or supplied to the inner Make command. Make should invoke Bazel whenever the archive is requested, allowing Bazel to check its own inputs. [Worker invocation](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/Makefile.work#L682-L781)

[P1] Sharing output_user_root can fail or abort builds
Both the system Bazel configuration and P4RT point to one output root under the default host-shared cache. This applies to P4RT even when the new container option is disabled. [System configuration](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/tools/bazel/slave.bazelrc#L12), [P4RT override](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/src/sonic-p4rt/Makefile#L30-L31)
Two failure cases follow from the pinned Bazel implementation:
- Different host users: the first user creates the output root; the second user’s Bazel process exits because its UID does not own that directory. Making the parent world-writable does not satisfy Bazel’s ownership check. [Bazel ownership check](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/6.4.0/src/main/cpp/blaze_util_posix.cc#L490-L521)
- Concurrent slaves using the same UID: default slaves mount each checkout at /sonic, so Bazel selects the same output base. Source tracing shows that separate PID namespaces can cause another server to start there; replacing the shared PID file can terminate the active server and abort its build. [Workspace mount](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/Makefile.work#L367-L372), [Bazel output-base selection](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/6.4.0/src/main/cpp/blaze.cc#L1334-L1340), [PID-file watcher](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/6.4.0/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/server/PidFileWatcher.java#L39-L107)
Give users and concurrent slaves isolated output roots. Both configuration paths need the change.

[P2] Bazel images lose the load targets required by Make consumers
Filtering Bazel images out of DOCKER_IMAGES also removes them from DOCKER_LOAD_TARGETS. The loader rule creates targets only for that explicit list. [Filtering](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/slave.mk#L1375-L1376), [Loader construction](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/slave.mk#L1591-L1608)
Once a release image uses Bazel, building its ordinary Make debug image—or another Make container that lists it in _LOAD_DOCKERS—requests target/<image>.gz-load and fails because no loader exists. Include the Bazel image lists when creating load targets. [Consumer prerequisites](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/slave.mk#L1523-L1528)

[P2] Existing cache directories are changed to mode 0777
The new shell expression evaluates as (test directory || create directory) && chmod. Consequently, chmod also runs when the directory already exists.
A user who points SONIC_BAZEL_CACHE_SOURCE at an existing mode-0700 directory has it changed to 0777 during Makefile parsing, even with the Bazel container option disabled. Preserve existing permissions and apply creation permissions only to newly created directories. [Cache setup](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/Makefile.work#L248-L249)

[P2] The Trixie guard misses configuration-file values
The guard is in the root Makefile, which does not read rules/config.user or rules/config.organization. The worker loads those files later and passes the resulting flag to the slave. Thus, setting the flag to y through configuration bypasses a restriction that the same CLI value triggers; direct worker invocations also bypass it. [Root guard](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/Makefile#L42-L49), [Configuration loading](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/Makefile.work#L167-L169)
Validate the effective configuration in the worker or slave. This is a confirmed enforcement gap; it does not mean every Bookworm phase necessarily runs a Bazel target.

I suggest four focused changes in this PR. The key design is: Make hands each requested container to Bazel, while Bazel owns dependency checking and caching.

1. Always let Bazel check the container

Add a normal phony prerequisite to both Bazel archive rules. Keep the .gz targets as real file targets. Current rules

.PHONY: FORCE_BAZEL
FORCE_BAZEL:

$(addprefix $(TARGET_PATH)/,$(SONIC_BAZEL_DOCKER_IMAGES)): $(TARGET_PATH)/%.gz: .platform FORCE_BAZEL \
	$$(addprefix $(TARGET_PATH)/,$$($$*.gz_BAZEL_BASE))
	$(HEADER)
	bazel run //dockers/$*:write_$*.gz $(LOG)
	$(FOOTER)

Apply the same prerequisite to the debug rule.

The writer must also:

  • Produce deterministic archive bytes, including compression metadata.
  • Leave the existing archive and its timestamp untouched when the bytes are identical.
  • Atomically replace the archive when its contents change.

This gives the intended behavior:

Situation | Result -- | -- No source changes | Bazel checks its graph; archive timestamp stays unchanged Source changes, same resulting contents | Bazel rebuilds affected actions; archive stays unchanged Container contents change | Archive is replaced; downstream image can rebuild

For developers, default the host cache to a user-owned location such as $HOME/.cache/sonic/bazel. For CI, configure a persistent directory dedicated to each runner UID.

Keep only these settings in slave.bazelrc:

common --repository_cache=/bazel_cache/repository_cache
common --disk_cache=/bazel_cache/disk_cache

Remove the shared output_user_root setting. I would also drop this PR’s P4RT Makefile hunk, preserving its existing manual /bazel override for users who explicitly configure it. Normal P4RT builds would inherit the persistent disk/repository caches and use slave-local output state. P4RT change

For directory preparation:

  • Move it from Make parsing into slave setup.
  • Create a missing user directory with mode 0700.
  • Preserve existing ownership and permissions.
  • If the configured directory is unusable, report that and run with local caches.

This retains cached action outputs across runs. A new slave still reconstructs its analysis and extracted workspace; that is the tradeoff for isolating server state. Bazel supports disk-cache reuse across checkouts. Bazel cache documentation

A persistent output root can be considered later, with an exclusive lock held for the entire slave lifetime.

3. Restore the existing Docker loaders

Add the Bazel groups to DOCKER_LOAD_TARGETS before its static pattern rule. Current loader list

DOCKER_LOAD_TARGETS += $(addsuffix -load,$(addprefix $(TARGET_PATH)/, \
	$(SONIC_BAZEL_DOCKER_IMAGES) \
	$(SONIC_BAZEL_DBG_DOCKER_IMAGES)))

The existing loader can then serve Make-built debug images and containers that depend on a Bazel-built base. Validate that the Bazel writer produces the archive format and image tags expected by docker-image-load.

4. Enforce the Trixie restriction inside the slave

Keep the root check for early CLI feedback, and add the authoritative check in slave.mk after configuration files are loaded:

ifeq ($(BUILD_WITH_BAZEL_WHEN_AVAILABLE),y)
ifneq ($(BLDENV),trixie)
$(error BUILD_WITH_BAZEL_WHEN_AVAILABLE=y requires a trixie slave)
endif
endif

That covers configuration-file values and direct worker invocations while preserving this PR’s current Trixie-only policy. Current root guard

For a future mixed-distro build, I would select Bazel only inside the Trixie slave and let other slaves continue using Make. That is a broader behavior change than closing this guard gap.

As for your concerns:
> [P1] Make can skip Bazel after source edits

I'm happy to apply your comments, but also please note that in the common case (`BAZEL_MIN_READINESS=true BLDENV=trixie make target/docker-sysmgr.gz`), the Make build will still overcache. Note that this also happens in the current Make-based targets.

The only way to make this not happen is to make the catch-all rule a `.PHONY`, and I think that is too big a change for this PR.

> [P1] Sharing output_user_root can fail or abort builds
> [P2] Existing cache directories are changed to mode 0777

> [P2] Bazel images lose the load targets required by Make consumers
> [P2] The Trixie guard misses configuration-file values

Also, please note that I've replaced the binary "is Bazel enabled" flag with the more nuanced "BAZEL_MIN_READINESS" toggle, so that users can decide whether they want to consume all available Bazel builds, or just the stable ones.
